$comment: The 2026-09-14 divergence, preserved so the fix can be tested against what
actually happened rather than against a memory of it.
NO THIRD-PARTY HTML IS STORED HERE. Every field is either a number this
repository produced, a message this repository's own code emitted, or a
measurement of a response (size, presence/absence) taken at the time. The
registry pages themselves are not ours to vendor.

localReviewedResult.$comment: Run from a residential IP on a tree byte-identical to origin/main. This is the reviewed truth: 12 genuine cfa:group findings plus 3 known AKC ones.

githubRunnerResult.$comment: Run 34853750161, same commit, GitHub-hosted runner. 182 of the 185 findings are CFA fields that the local run did not produce.

repeatedCfaFailureCategories.$comment: Every CFA finding on the runner carried one of exactly six messages. Two of them hit 45 of 45 CFA records — the uniformity is the tell: 45 independent editorial changes do not land in one week, and they do not all land on breeds whose pages read correctly from another network.

categories.message: no standard PDF on the page
class no longer named on the page
the cited field and value are not on the page
no sentence on the page ties that year to recognition
quoted weight wording not found on the page
quoted coat wording not found on the page

controlBreeds.$comment: Three CFA pages read from a residential IP on 2026-09-14, chosen because they separate a real finding from a fetch artefact. If a change makes Abyssinian and Siamese stop disagreeing, or makes American Bobtail start, it has broken the check rather than fixed it. Byte counts are ranges: repeated fetches of the same URL minutes apart differed by up to 10%, which is why the plausibility floor is an order of magnitude below the smallest.

measuredRealPageShape.$comment: Six live CFA breed pages sampled 2026-09-14 from a residential IP. These numbers, not a guess, set CFA_MIN_BYTES. Note ambientMarkers: a captcha widget is present on every ordinary CFA page, which is why captcha presence can never be a block signal.

$comment: The hypothesis, tested. The verifier WITHOUT the plausibility gate was run
against a stub serving nothing but a Cloudflare-style interstitial for every
CFA URL. It reproduced the runner's by-field breakdown exactly — all five
fields, all five counts. A bot challenge is therefore sufficient to explain
the entire 182-finding CFA incident; no editorial change at CFA is needed to
account for any part of it.
This does NOT prove the runner received a Cloudflare challenge specifically.
It proves that an interstitial of this class produces precisely this output,
and that the gate removes it.
